label: GO: choosing a1 after an unrewarded trial that did not end in S1 (early/mid episode)
explanation: Fires only at GO (0 on D1/D2), almost exclusively when the previous trial was unrewarded (99.8% of mass) and the agent is choosing a1 (model_act==1, 97% of mass; high positive choice logit). It never fires after an unrewarded visit to S1 (prev_state==1); the typical case is a1 -> S2 rare unrewarded, followed by staying with a1 (the model-based stay response), plus a2 -> S2 common unrewarded followed by a switch to a1. In short: an unrewarded S2 outcome pushing the agent toward a1. Activation is also gated by time in episode: frequent early, decaying, zero from trial ~80 on (ep_trial<75 raises dev precision from 0.61 to 0.81). Magnitude is near-binary (median 1.0); weaker activations show up at the edges (e.g. lower choice logit or a2 choices). Does not fire after rewarded trials or on a2 choices except rarely. model_act is the agent own policy output at GO, so no future variable is used. Dev: P 0.81, R 0.89, F1 0.85, mass recall 0.97.

issues: The factual claims hold up. On dev, the feature is active only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps). prev_reward==0 carries 99.8% of the activation mass and model_act==1 carries 97.4%. The predicate (GO & prev_reward==0 & prev_state==1) has 0 recall, so it truly never fires after an unrewarded S1 visit. Activity is zero from trial 80 on (only 536 active steps in trials 70-79). Median magnitude is 1.0.
The case breakdown is right. Within the predicate, a1 leading to S2 by a rare transition holds 70% of the mass (precision 0.90). a2 leading to S2 by the common transition holds 8% (precision 0.71).

About 19% of the mass sits on rel -3, the first trial of each window, where prev_state is -1 (unknown in the window). There the predicate's precision is only 0.64, against 0.87 on the other trials, because some of those unseen previous trials ended in S1. This is a limit of the window data, not a gap in the label. Still, 'did not end in S1' cannot be checked for that fifth of the activations.

The episode-position effect is a soft fade, not a hard cutoff. With prev_state==2, precision is 1.00 for trials 0-39, 0.91 for 40-59, 0.48 for 60-74 and about 0 from 75 on. Most of the false positives that remain on trials with a known previous state fall in the 60-74 fade zone. A cutoff of ep_trial < 70 does slightly better than < 75 (test F1 0.852 vs 0.836).

Minor: precision is lower (0.75) when the trial two back was also unrewarded, meaning a run of losses, against 0.93 when it was rewarded. So the feature fires more reliably on a loss that follows a reward. This is a modulation of firing strength, not a counterexample class.
The predicate uses no future variables: model_act is the agent's own output at GO.
